The plan is a proper taper and nothing in it is unsafe. Running days are 5, 5 (with a short sharpener at goal pace), 4 and 2 miles, with rest on Monday and Friday as usual, and every day can be run as written. The race pacing fits a sub-3:45 goal (about 8:35/mi), with a conservative first two miles at 8:40 to 8:45.

What keeps it from a 5:
- The specific numbers (easy runs at 9:52/mi and 139 bpm, the 20-17-20 long runs, Sunday's 12 miles) aren't on the card, so I can't check them, though they may come from her log.
- Her 'heavy, flat, dead' legs aren't named as normal taper legs in the visible text, and that's the main thing she reported about her body this week.

Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 53, 40, 42, 46 mi
This week: 34 mi over 5 runs.
Body: "Legs heavy and flat. Nothing hurts, they just feel dead."
Feeling: "Nervous. I feel like I'm losing fitness."
Asks: "Is it crazy to do one more 16-miler on Wednesday so I feel ready?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: Your training is done, and last week went exactly to plan. …

Your easy runs have held at about 9:52/mi and 139 bpm for a month. (3) Your confidence should come from the work you've already done. You ran two 20-milers in the last five weeks, with a 17 between them.
